reason: E1 shows that thermal exposure of a similar HEA coating on steel at 800°C forms a Cr2O3 and spinel oxide layer that enhances wear resistance, supporting the first two premises. However, E1 uses a 10-week exposure, not 2 hours, and E2 reports wear data at room temperature, not 800°C, so the specific annealing conditions, high-temperature wear performance, and quantitative 50% reduction are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Thermal exposure of FeNiCrCoCu coating on steel forms a dual-layer oxide scale of Cr2O3 and (Fe,Co,Ni,Cu)3O4 spinel
This dual-layer oxide scale enhances wear resistance
Annealing at 750°C for 2 hours in air is sufficient to form this dual-layer scale
The dual-layer scale reduces wear by minimizing metal-to-metal contact and providing solid lubrication
A 50% reduction in wear rate is expected at 800°C under 15 N load
